summary: R7 governance/integrity hardening tested end-to-end. Backend: 17/17 core tests pass (auth gate, exceptions register, buyer classification + SoD 403 negative + positive verify by legal_counsel and by a second admin (owner) with override -> exception row, integrity raise/review/resolve/senior-override (422 short reason, 403 for committee_member, exception kind=integrity_override written, 409 review after override), collusion on empty/real notice, fee waiver maker-checker 403 + approve by owner -> exception kind=fee_waiver, reject path writes no exception, 409 on re-decide, legal register upsert by legal+admin (single row), 403 for committee, incidents create/resolve + public no-auth endpoint with SLA, private incident hidden). AI price-leak: the Price line is gone from _fetch_bid_scope (checked in source). Two loophole probes FAIL: (1) a committee member can resolve a case after a senior override, which silently replaces 'overridden'; (2) a verified buyer classification can be overwritten back to pending by anyone with admin/reviewer, which wipes the verifier record. Frontend: login -> sidebar 'Governance & integrity' -> all 6 tabs render; buyer classify form saves and the row appears; Verify by the same admin shows the SoD error toast; fee waiver self-approve shows the SoD error toast; collusion scan, raise case, legal save and incident log/resolve all work.

critical.issue: No status guard. After a senior override (status=overridden), a committee member can still call resolve, and it replaces status/resolution (overridden -> upheld). The UI then shows UPHELD next to the override text. The audited override can be undone without its own exception entry. Reproduced in tests/test_r7_governance_loopholes.py::test_resolve_after_override_should_be_blocked (returns 200, expected 409). Fix: reject resolve when status is not open/under_review. Consider requiring at least one review before resolving.

Unconditional upsert by notice_ref. A VERIFIED classification is overwritten back to pending_verification, and verified_by/verified_at/verify_note are cleared, with no history and no exception logged. It also lets a second person become classified_by on another person's entry, so the original classifier can then verify their own buyer type: A classifies X, B reclassifies X, A verifies. That is an SoD bypass. Reproduced in test_reclassify_after_verify_by_other_user (returns 200). Fix: block reclassification of verified rows (409), or require a recorded exception, and keep a history array.

minor.issue: notice_ref is never checked against db.notices, so classifications/cases can be created for notices that do not exist.
Can be applied repeatedly or to an already-resolved case. Each call adds another exception row; there is no status check.
The docstring still says 'company_name + price + technical_notes'. The code is correct, but the docstring is misleading for auditors.
documents: List[dict] is not validated. approved_by is set even when legal_status is pending/blocked (it should be updated_by).

ui_bugs.issue: A hard reload or direct URL load of /admin/e/governance sends you to /login?expired=1 (the token is kept in memory). It works through client-side navigation. This appears to be existing app-wide behaviour, not new.

issues: The success toast after a status update shows the raw word 'resolved' in lowercase; use 'Incident resolved'.
Some buttons have no data-testid: buyer Reject, fee waiver Reject, incident Monitoring, integrity Vote uphold/dismiss and Resolve uphold/dismiss.

action_items: Block /integrity-cases/resolve (and /review) when status is not open/under_review, so the senior override cannot be undone silently
Make /buyer-classifications reject reclassifying a verified row (409), or record it as an exception with history; stop the classifier-swap SoD bypass
Optionally validate that notice_ref exists; block repeat senior overrides
Add the missing data-testids for Reject/Monitoring/Vote/Resolve buttons; fix the bids_ai_compare docstring
critical_code_review_comments: SoD checks compare emails case-insensitively and are correct for verify/decide, but the classify upsert opens a bypass (see critical #2)
The integrity workflow has no state machine: resolve and override accept any status
record_exception writes to manual_exceptions and to audit_log, which is good; _out() strips _id (checked: no _id in responses)
The public incidents endpoint correctly exposes only safe fields (no created_by/impact)

rca of the issue: resolve_integrity_case does an unconditional $set without checking rec.status. classify_buyer uses update_one(upsert=True) with a $set that resets status/verified_by on every call, regardless of the existing state.
